title: Choir and Ember
premise: Zephyrine Dunmore has spent his life carving bones in the valley of Hollowmere, where a ancient ward suppresses all magic—and where his gift for hearing the dead goes mercifully quiet. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands and whispers that the King of Cael Adair is already dead, replaced by something that wears his crown, Zephyrine's valley sanctuary becomes a target. Hunted by the Ember Choir—the crown's order of song-mages who bind souls into service—he must cross a winter-hardened kingdom carrying the map to the king's true resting place. There he learns the dead king's spirit can be called back to unseat the usurper, but only if someone willingly lends it their voice: a bargain that will cost the speaker their own identity. In the frozen throne room, Zephyrine gives the dead king his voice, unbinding the crown-thing at the cost of forgetting who he was—until the people he saved speak his name back to him, rebuilding him from loyalty rather than magic.
about_author: Mara Yarrow is the pen name of a former funeral singer from the northern coast who claims she wrote her first novel on the backs of hymn programs. She lives quietly with too many candles and a firm belief that every story is a séance.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. We meet him carving memorial bones for the dying in Hollowmere, where the ward keeps both magic and his unwanted gift silent. He is content, or tells himself so. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of a man hiding from what he is.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A half-frozen courier collapses at the valley ford, raving about a crown and a choir. With his last breath he presses a bone-handled map into Zephyrine's hands. Emotional beat: dread—the ward flickers as the stranger dies, and Zephyrine hears his first dead voice in years.

chapters.title: What the Dead Courier Said
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The corpse whispers its final message: the king is dead, the thing on the throne eats souls, and the map must reach the Ashen Crypt before midwinter. The ward begins failing; magic seeps back into the valley. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Burns Its Bridges
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with interludes from Elder Maren. The valley elders, fearing retribution, vote to expel him rather than shelter a marked man. His childhood friend Tam offers to come along and is refused. Emotional beat: betrayal and exile—the first cost of the map.

chapters.title: The First Song on the Wind
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the mountain road he hears distant choral harmonies that make his bones ache—the Ember Choir sweeping the passes, listening through song for resonant souls. He learns to walk deaf, plugging his ears with wax and carved silence. Emotional beat: hunted paranoia.

chapters.title: The Town That Sang Along
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the market town of Bellharrow, everyone hums the Choir's liturgy without knowing why; the songs are laced with obedience. An old woman recognizes the map's seal and begs him to burn it. Emotional beat: horror at soft, comfortable corruption.

chapters.title: Tam Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Zephyrine and Tam. Tam followed anyway, and saves Zephyrine from a Choir scout—but Zephyrine catches Tam humming the liturgy under his breath. Loyalty frays against suspicion. Emotional beat: the ache of doubting someone you love.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Craft
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered by scouts, Zephyrine discovers his carvings can hold and redirect the dead's voices—a weapon he never wanted. He fells the scouts with a chorus of the betrayed. Emotional beat: power tasted for the first time, and liked more than he admits.

chapters.title: Vespera of the Choir
chapters.summary: Vespera's POV introduced. The Choir's youngest cantor senses an 'unbound voice' moving north and requests the hunt herself, hiding her doubts about what the Choir does with captured souls. Emotional beat: a mirror antagonist—also gifted, also used.

chapters.title: Crossing the Weeping Moors
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Tam's POV. The moors are thick with unquiet dead who mistake Zephyrine for a rescuer. He promises them rest if they guide him past the Choir's cordon—a promise he may not be able to keep. Emotional beat: compassion weaponized, guilt accruing.

chapters.title: The Map's Second Secret
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. By firelight, the map reveals hidden script: the Ashen Crypt holds not just the king's body but the original binding-song that made the crown-thing possible. Whoever holds it could make another. Emotional beat: temptation—the map is power, not just duty.

chapters.title: Ambush at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Tam's POV. Vespera's squad corners them; Tam takes a singing-wound meant for Zephyrine, his voice literally stolen. Zephyrine escapes only by unleashing the moor-dead, breaking his promise of rest. Emotional beat: grief and self-loathing; the cost mounts.

chapters.title: Winter Falls Early
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Snow seals the high passes; the long winter of legend begins, exactly as the dead foretold. Sheltering in a shepherd's bothy, Zephyrine nearly burns the map to save himself the journey. Emotional beat: despair at its lowest ebb.

chapters.title: The Cantor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vespera's POV. Sent to recover Tam's stolen voice from the Choir's vaults, Vespera sees the soul-harvest firsthand and understands what the crown-thing truly feeds on. She defects, taking Tam with her. Emotional beat: conscience outranking loyalty.

chapters.title: Three Voices in the Snow
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Vespera finds Zephyrine; knives first, then truth. Together they plan the crypt approach while teaching mute Tam to speak again through one of Zephyrine's carved bones. Emotional beat: unlikely fellowship forged in shared betrayal by the same master.

chapters.title: The Ashen Crypt
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They descend beneath the ruined abbey and find the dead king, Aldric, still lucid after ten years of death—held together by sheer refusal. He explains the price: a living voice lent willingly, and forgotten by the lender. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror at the bargain.

chapters.title: Who Gives Their Voice
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Each weighs the sacrifice: Vespera argues her trained voice would serve best; Tam writes that he owes a debt. Zephyrine realizes only his gift can hold two souls in one throat. He decides alone, and lies to the others about when. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen in secret.

chapters.title: The Long Climb to Cael Adair
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The three cross the frozen capital's outskirts during the coronation-feast, slipping in among mummers. Zephyrine practices surrendering his memories, saying goodbye to his own name in his head. Emotional beat: tender, elegiac preparation for self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Throne Room of the Crown-Thing
chapters.summary: Climax, shared POV. Confrontation with the usurper, which reveals itself as the first binding-song given flesh, wearing kings like coats. Vespera countersings the Choir's liturgy; Tam shatters the resonance-glass; Zephyrine opens his throat to dead King Aldric. Emotional beat: desperate, blazing defiance.

chapters.title: One Voice, Two Souls
chapters.summary: Climax continued, Zephyrine/Aldric shared voice. Aldric sings the unbinding through Zephyrine's mouth while the crown-thing tears at Zephyrine's memories to stop him. He forgets his mother, the valley, his name—and keeps singing. The thing unravels; Aldric's spirit departs at peace. Emotional beat: annihilation transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: The Name Spoken Back
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. A hollowed Zephyrine sits amid the aftermath until Tam speaks his name, then Vespera, then the freed courtiers—each memory returned not by magic but by testimony. He remembers being loved before he remembers anything else. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt through loyalty and truth.

chapters.title: Carving Bones in a Louder World
chapters.summary: Resolution, Zephyrine's POV. Spring comes; Aldric's heir offers Zephyrine a place dismantling the Choir's bindings. Instead he returns toward Hollowmere with Tam and Vespera, carrying the binding-song to be buried where no one can sing it. He hears the dead now everywhere—but they ask only to be remembered. Emotional beat: homecoming changed but whole; power refused, identity kept.
